note: Checked Nov 28: Georgia district and state AI policy, AI in education, open grants, funding risk and new-client leads. Nothing new verified in the last 14 days, so earlier items still in their windows were kept. The LEGO NSF AI-Ready America grant (due 2026-05-07) and Georgia BOOST (2025-26 cycle) pages show only closed cycles, so they were left out. Toshiba grant deadline is Dec 1.

items.title: Google says schools that turn off AI Overviews will lose Google Search access
items.why: Schools that stay fully AI-free may lose Search for students, which pushes districts toward guided, teacher-led AI use. Tell principals your classes teach students to question and check AI answers with a teacher present, and offer that as the controlled option. The article gives no start date or grade range, so do not quote either.

items.title: Rockdale school board asks about timeline for student AI-ethics training
items.why: At its Nov. 12 work session the Rockdale board asked when students will get AI-ethics training, so the district is looking for it. Email the Rockdale curriculum or technology director offering a short, teacher-guided AI literacy and ethics class, and cite the board's own question.

items.title: Society for Science STEM Action Grants: small grants for community STEM nonprofits
items.why: A $5,000 grant could fund a season of your classes if a nonprofit partner applies. Send the link to a youth organization or library you work with and offer to write the program section; applications open in December.
items.amount: Up to $5,000 per grant, renewable up to 3 years
items.who: Nonprofit organizations working to increase public participation in STEM
items.verify: Page lists no detailed eligibility. Check the About & FAQ page, and whether a for-profit studio can apply directly or must partner with a nonprofit.

items.title: Atlanta Public Schools holds community conversation on AI policy for students and parents
items.why: A metro district is publicly debating student AI rules. Districts nearby will likely follow, so frame your classes as teacher-guided, objective-based AI literacy with no sensitive student data entered, and offer that language to Newton, Rockdale and Clayton decision makers.

items.title: Georgia students raise privacy concerns over Meta AI smart glasses; state law bans such devices in schools
items.why: Student privacy and recording are live issues with Georgia families and schools. Add a short data-privacy and device-use statement to your program overview so administrators see you are ahead of the concern.

items.title: Georgia colleges add mandatory AI coursework while worrying students over-rely on AI
items.why: Colleges now require AI classes and stress critical thinking over tool use. Use this in pitches: your program builds the thinking skills and basic AI literacy students need before college.

items.title: Toshiba America Foundation: grades 6-12 STEM project grants
items.why: Teachers apply, you supply the project. Send to your NCSA and NCCA contacts: a teacher can request funds to bring you in.
items.who: Grade 6-12 educators (not stated for schools or nonprofits)
items.verify: Listing gives Nov 1 and Dec 1, 2026 without saying which tier. Check the funder page.
